# Taurine

Fast, secure, and easy-to-use text expander and keyboard automation tool built in Rust. Taurine allows users to manage local text expansions via a robust CLI and background service.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ereinaimer/taurine/refs/heads/main/README.md)
- [Contributing Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ereinaimer/taurine/refs/heads/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [License](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ereinaimer/taurine/refs/heads/main/LICENSE)
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/Kc9XmHJgsS)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/ereinaimer/taurine)

---

## 1. Installation

Taurine is currently in development. You can build it from source using the Rust toolchain:

### 1.1 Requirements
*   Rust (latest stable version)
*   Cargo (included with Rust)

### 1.2 Building from Source
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ereinaimer/taurine.git
cd taurine

# Build the project
cargo build --release

# The binary will be located at ./target/release/taurine
```

---

## 2. Quick-Start (CLI)

| Command | Action | One-liner |
|---------|--------|-----------|
| **up** | Start the automation service | taurine up |
| **add** | Create a new text expansion | taurine add "trigger" "output" |
| **ls** | List expansions (supports --sort) | taurine ls --sort usage --desc |
| **config** | Manage system settings | taurine config ls |
| **status** | Check background daemon health | taurine status |
| **down** | Stop the automation service | taurine down |

---

## 3. Command Reference

### 3.1 Managing the Service
*   taurine up: Installs and starts the background service. Use taurine down to stop it.
*   taurine restart: Restarts the service to apply changes or refresh the engine.
*   taurine status: Reports whether the engine is online and if it's currently paused.

### 3.2 Managing Automations
*   taurine add <trigger> <output>: Adds a new snippet. Triggers are typically prefixed with a special character (default is `>`).
*   taurine delete <trigger>: Removes an automation matching the specific trigger.
*   taurine ls: Displays a formatted table of all active triggers.
    *   **Sorting**: Use --sort with alpha, usage, created, or recent.
    *   **Order**: Use --asc or --desc (default is ascending for alpha, descending for others).

### 3.3 Configuration
*   taurine config set <key> <value>: Updates a specific setting.
*   taurine config reset <key>: Resets a setting to factory defaults (use --all to reset everything).
*   Key Settings: trigger_char, pause_hotkey, start_on_boot.

---

## 4. Example Automations

Practical templates for every major Taurine feature, organized by integration pattern:

### 4.1 Basic Snippets
*   Git Shortcut: >gs -> git status
*   Common Phrase: >ty -> Thank you for your response!
*   Code Bracket: >cur -> {\n    \n} (Standard expansion)

### 4.2 Dynamic Snippets (With Arguments)
Snippets can take arguments passed within double quotes after the trigger.
*   Positional Args: >repo-"ereinaimer, taurine" -> https://github.com/ereinaimer/taurine
    *   Snippet template: https://github.com/{0}/{1}
*   Named Args & Defaults: >gh-"username=ereinaimer" -> https://github.com/ereinaimer/taurine
    *   Snippet template: https://github.com/{username}/{repo=taurine}

### 4.3 System Variables
*   Contextual:
    *   >hi -> {time.greeting}, {clipboard}! How can I help you?
    *   >fn -> pub fn name() {\n    {cursor}\n}
*   Generators:
    *   >uuid -> ID: {uuid.v7}
    *   >today -> Fixed on: {date.iso}
    *   >log -> [{time.full}] {env.USER}: {clipboard}
*   Environment:
    *   >path -> Home: {env.HOME} (Unix) or Home: {env.USERPROFILE} (Windows)
*   Keystroke Sequences:
    *   >login -> admin{key.tab}password123{key.enter}
    *   >select -> {key.ctrl+a}{key.backspace} (Use `mod` for cross-platform: {key.mod+a})
    *   >slow -> Start...{delay.500ms}End.

### 4.4 Inline Math (Instant Calculation)
Math expansion works with any trigger character followed by a valid expression.
*   Arithmetic: >15*4 -> 60
*   Scientific: >sqrt(16) -> 4 | >2pi -> 6.2832
*   Precedence: >(100-25)/3 -> 25 (BEDMAS compliant)
*   Scientific Notation: >1.2e3 -> 1200

### 4.5 Hybrid Templates
*   Commit Message: >cmt -> feat({env.PWD}): {clipboard}\n\nSigned-off-by: {env.USER}
*   Daily Log: >day -> # {date.long}\n- Started at {time.now.12h} in {env.COMPUTERNAME}\n- {cursor}

### 4.6 Text Transformers
*   Basic Literal: >greet -> {upper.'welcome'} -> WELCOME
*   Direct Variable: >user -> {title.name} (Formats the name argument in Title Case)
*   System Variable: >now -> {upper.time.now} -> 12:00 PM (Uppercases the current time)
*   Deep Chaining: >id -> {shoutysnake.uuid.v4} -> A1B2-C3D4... (Uppercases and snakes the UUID)

---

## 5. Dynamic Variables

Taurine supports rich, dynamic content injection using the {variable} syntax. System variables are divided into three core categories:

### 5.1 Content Generators
Generators produce and inject new content into your expansions. Most support sub-formats via dot-notation (e.g., {date.iso}).

*   Date ({date.*}):
    *   Formats: date.iso (YYYY-MM-DD), date.short (MM/DD/YYYY), date.long (Month DD, YYYY).
    *   Components: date.weekday, date.year, date.month, date.month_name, date.day.
    *   Modifiers: Supports .tomorrow and .yesterday prefixes (e.g., {date.tomorrow.iso}).
*   Time ({time.*}):
    *   Current: time.now (HH:mm), time.full (HH:mm:ss).
    *   Formatting: Supports .12h and .24h modifiers (e.g., {time.now.12h}).
    *   Utility: time.greeting (Context-aware), time.epoch (Unix timestamp), time.utc, time.tz (Offset).
*   UUID ({uuid.*}):
    *   Standards: uuid.v4 (Random), uuid.v7 (Time-ordered).
    *   Compact: uuid.simple (32-character hex, no dashes).
*   Environment ({env.*}):
    *   Usage: {env.<VAR_NAME>} resolves to any available system environment variable (e.g., {env.USER}).

### 5.2 Contextual Variables
Contextual variables pull data from the active system state at the moment of expansion.

*   Clipboard ({clipboard}):
    *   Operation: Captures the current system clipboard content and injects it into the expansion.
    *   Safety: The daemon captures the clipboard state *before* any expansion actions to ensure the data is preserved accurately.

### 5.3 Expansion Directives
Directives are special placeholders that do not produce text themselves but control the behavior of the expansion process (keystrokes, timing, and positioning).

*   Keystroke ({key.*}):
    *   Aliases: Single keys like tab, enter, esc, up, down, home, end, backspace, space.
    *   Alphabets/Numbers: key.a..key.z, key.0..key.9, key.f1..key.f12.
    *   Combinations: Supports + separator for modifier chords (e.g., {key.ctrl+shift+t}).
    *   Platform Modifiers: mod (Cmd on macOS, Win/Ctrl elsewhere), win, cmd, opt.
*   Delay ({delay.*}):
    *   Usage: {delay.Xms} (e.g., {delay.200ms}) pauses the expansion sequence for exactly X milliseconds.
    *   Utility: Essential for waiting for UI transitions or target applications to process field changes.
*   Cursor ({cursor}):
    *   Action: Defines the final caret (cursor) position after expansion is complete.
    *   Mechanism: The engine calculates the required left-arrow offset and automatically simulates the necessary back-arrow keystrokes.
    *   Conflict Rule: If a snippet contains any {key.*} directives, the {cursor} tag is ignored as a directive (treated as literal text) to avoid ambiguous positioning in multi-action sequences.

### 5.4 Text Transformers ({transformer.*})
Transformers modify the casing and structure of provided content (literals or variables) using dot-notation.

*   Flattened Resolution: Resolve content directly without nesting braces (e.g., {upper.msg} resolves msg first, then uppercases it).
*   Literal Handling: Supports literal strings wrapped in single or double quotes (e.g., {upper.'hello'}).
*   Recursive Chaining: Apply multiple modifiers in a single tag (e.g., {upper.lower.val}).
*   Format List:
    *   Case Styles: upper, lower, title, camel, pascal.
    *   Delimiters: snake, kebab, shoutysnake, shoutykebab, train.

---

## 6. Inline Math Expansion

Taurine can automatically evaluate mathematical expressions typed directly into any text field. Expansion occurs when the input buffer contains a valid math expression prefixed by the **trigger character** (e.g., >5+5 -> 10).

### 6.1 Math Parser Capabilities
*   BEDMAS Compliance: Standard order of operations (Brackets, Exponents, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction).
*   Scientific Notation: Support for large/small numbers (e.g., 1.2e10 or 5E-3).
*   Operators: Supports +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ (exponent).
*   Implicit Multiplication: Automatically resolves expressions like 2(3+4) as 2 * (3 + 4).
*   Constants & Functions:
    *   Constants: pi, e.
    *   Functions: sqrt(x), abs(x), floor(x), ceil(x), round(x).

---

## 7. Hot Reload Support

Taurine features a robust "Hot Reload" mechanism to ensure your productivity is never interrupted:
*   Instant Sync: Every time an automation is added, updated, or deleted, the daemon automatically reloads its in-memory lookup cache.
*   Settings Persistence: Updating application settings (e.g., trigger_char) triggers an immediate state synchronization without requiring a manual restart of the service.

---

## 8. Future Roadmap

We are committed to making Taurine the most accessible keyboard automation tool:
*   Cross-Platform UI: A simple, unified interface built with Flutter for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
*   Fuzzy Search Overlay: A global command palette (powered by the Flutter UI) to help users discover and execute their automations instantly, removing the need to memorize every trigger prefix.

---

## 9. Project Architecture

Taurine is a modular Rust workspace designed for absolute performance and safety.
* core: Foundations, database layer (rusqlite storing JSON settings), and the custom interpolation/math engine.
* cli: Front-facing tool (clap) and OS service manager.
* daemon: Background logic responsible for keyboard monitoring and text injection.
    * Windows/macOS: Uses rdev for global hooks.
    * Linux (Wayland/X11): Bypasses display servers entirely using evdev (listening) and uinput (injecting).
    * IPC: The CLI and Daemon communicate strictly via gRPC (tonic).
* tui: Interactive terminal interface (currently under development).

---

## 10. System Paths

Taurine stores data and logs in platform-specific local directories:

| Platform | Path |
|----------|------|
| Windows | %LOCALAPPDATA%\Taurine |
| Linux | ~/.local/share/taurine |
| macOS | ~/Library/Application Support/Taurine |

*   Database: taurine.db (Primary SQLite storage).
*   Logs: logs/ (Daily rotating log files).

---

## 11. AI Agent Best Practices & Coding Guidelines

When assisting with Taurine's codebase or usage, strictly adhere to these rules:
1.  User Interaction: Use the taurine CLI commands directly for automation management. Do not suggest manual edits to taurine.db.
2.  Linux Permissions: Never suggest X11 tools (xdotool, xmodmap) or running the daemon as root. Taurine achieves kernel-level Wayland support by applying capabilities to the binary (sudo setcap 'cap_dac_override+ep'). The daemon drops these privileges after acquiring file descriptors.
3.  Error Handling: Use color-eyre for application-level error reporting and tracing for all logging.
4.  Performance: Prefer zero-copy string references (&str) over allocations (String) in the hot path of the FastBuffer keystroke evaluator.
